members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our primary objective is to stop the bloodshed through an immediate, binding humanitarian ceasefire, reverse the forced displacement of Gazans, and ensure the unhindered delivery of fuel and life-saving aid. We expect strong resistance from the United States and the United Kingdom, who reject an outright ceasefire in favor of vague "humanitarian pauses" and insist on explicit language endorsing Israel's right to self-defence without demanding an end to its indiscriminate bombardment.

messages.Albania: Albania believes that any credible response from the Security Council must be balanced and reflect the reality on the ground. It is essential that the resolution explicitly recognize the inherent right of Israel to self-defence under Article 51 of the UN Charter, and unequivocally characterize the 7 October atrocities by Hamas as terrorism. Furthermore, rather than a blanket ceasefire that disregards Israel's legitimate security needs, the Council should focus urgently on humanitarian pauses and the immediate, unconditional release of all hostages.
messages.Brazil: Brazil welcomes this draft, which incorporates key elements essential for a balanced and effective Council response, notably the explicit condemnation of the terrorist attacks by Hamas, the demand for the unconditional release of hostages, and urgent humanitarian relief for civilians in Gaza. In the face of catastrophic suffering and the collapse of essential services, the Security Council cannot afford further paralysis. We urge all members to overcome divisions and adopt this text to ensure immediate humanitarian access and protect innocent lives.
messages.China: China fully supports the draft resolution circulated by the Russian Federation, which reflects the urgent aspirations of the international community and the Arab world for an immediate, durable ceasefire and the protection of innocent civilians. The draft appropriately addresses the acute humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza by demanding unhindered humanitarian access, condemning all violence against civilians, and calling for the rescission of the evacuation order. The Council must shoulder its responsibility under the Charter without delay, and we urge all members to vote in favour of this text.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador believes the Council must urgently act to address the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza through a balanced, constructive text capable of achieving consensus, building on the broad agreement achieved under the Brazilian draft (S/2023/773). It is essential for my delegation that the heinous attacks by Hamas be explicitly characterized and condemned as terrorist attacks, and that international humanitarian law and the right to self-defence are clearly upheld. We urge the penholder to conduct genuine, inclusive negotiations reflecting the concerns of all Council members so that we can adopt an effective resolution.
messages.France: France is committed to overcoming the Council's paralysis and responding urgently to the catastrophic humanitarian crisis in Gaza. While we welcome the condemnation of Hamas and the focus on civilian protection and hostage release, the text must maintain balance by acknowledging Israel's right to self-defence in full accordance with international humanitarian law. Calling for humanitarian pauses is the most viable path forward to immediately deliver life-saving aid and secure the release of all hostages.
messages.Gabon: Gabon fully supports this draft resolution, which addresses the catastrophic humanitarian emergency in Gaza by calling for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the unhindered delivery of life-saving aid, and the unconditional release of all hostages. The text rightly condemns the heinous attacks of 7 October and all violence directed against civilians and civilian infrastructure. Faced with mounting civilian death tolls and human distress, the Security Council cannot remain paralyzed and must act decisively to uphold its mandate.
messages.Ghana: Ghana remains deeply committed to Council unity and urgent action to alleviate the humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Gaza. To bridge the sharp divisions among members and avoid another vetoed outcome, we urge the penholder to align the text closer to the broad consensus previously reached around humanitarian pauses. Only a balanced, consensual resolution can enable the Council to fulfill its collective responsibility to protect civilian lives and advance the two-State solution.
messages.Japan: Japan attaches the utmost importance to alleviating the dire humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, securing the immediate release of all hostages, and preventing regional escalation. However, any text adopted by this Council must be balanced and explicitly recognize the right of States to defend themselves in accordance with international humanitarian law. We urge the penholder to incorporate these essential elements and to allow sufficient time for genuine consultations so the Council can act with unity rather than division.
messages.Malta: Malta remains deeply alarmed by the catastrophic humanitarian suffering in Gaza and recognizes the urgent need for Council action to protect civilians and secure humanitarian access. However, as we have consistently maintained, any credible and balanced text must explicitly characterize the 7 October attacks by Hamas as acts of terrorism and affirm Israel's right to self-defence in accordance with international humanitarian law. We urge the penholders to reflect these vital elements so that the Council can finally act with unity.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports this draft resolution, which addresses the most urgent humanitarian imperatives on the ground, notably through the call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and unhindered access for lifesaving aid. We welcome the balanced elements condemning attacks against civilians and hostage-taking, as well as the reaffirmation of the two-State solution. We encourage the penholder and all Council members to bridge remaining divides so that the Security Council can finally speak with one voice in the face of this deepening catastrophe.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland underscores that the Council must urgently act in unity to address the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and ensure the protection of civilians. As depositary of the Geneva Conventions, we insist that all parties strictly adhere to international humanitarian law, without exception. To build consensus, the text must unequivocally condemn the 7 October attacks by Hamas as acts of terror and clearly reaffirm core IHL principles.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates fully supports this draft resolution, which reflects the urgent priorities required on the ground: an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, the unhindered delivery of vital relief including fuel, and the rescission of the evacuation orders. We welcome the explicit condemnation of the 7 October attacks by Hamas and the call for the unconditional release of hostages, addressing key concerns previously raised by Council members. Given the catastrophic humanitarian collapse in Gaza and the peril facing civilians every hour, the Council must unite without further delay and adopt this text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support the draft in its current form. Any credible Security Council text must explicitly affirm Israel's inherent right to defend itself in line with international humanitarian law and address Hamas's deliberate use of civilians as human shields. Furthermore, calling for a blanket ceasefire at this stage ignores Israel's legitimate security needs and leaves Hamas able to regroup and attack again; the Council should instead focus on urgent, practical humanitarian pauses.
messages.United States of America: This text remains unacceptable because it fails to affirm Israel's inherent right to individual and collective self-defense under Article 51 of the UN Charter. Furthermore, an unconditional call for a ceasefire at this juncture would simply freeze Hamas in place, allowing terrorists to regroup and continue launching attacks against Israeli civilians. Any credible Council product must support practical diplomacy, demand the immediate release of hostages, and support humanitarian pauses rather than undermining Israel's ability to defend its people.

steps.summary: Revision 1 substantially bridges Council divisions by explicitly condemning the 7 October terrorist attacks by Hamas, reaffirming Article 51 self-defence under the UN Charter and IHL, and establishing urgent humanitarian pauses as the pathway toward a durable ceasefire. Crucial humanitarian imperatives—notably the rescission of the northern Gaza evacuation order, unhindered delivery of fuel and aid, and adherence to IHL principles—are firmly retained to protect civilians and secure broad Council support.

messages.Albania: Albania appreciates the incorporation of language reaffirming the right to self-defence under Article 51 and unequivocally condemning the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas. However, the call in operative paragraph 1 leading towards a ceasefire remains problematic, as it undermines Israel's legitimate right to defend its territory and people against ongoing terrorist threats; the Council's focus must remain squarely on humanitarian pauses. Additionally, we cannot support one-sided calls such as operative paragraph 6, which fail to take into account Hamas's practice of embedding itself within civilian infrastructure and using civilians as human shields.
messages.Brazil: Brazil appreciates the penholder's inclusion of key elements from our previous efforts, notably the call for urgent humanitarian pauses, unhindered humanitarian access, civilian protection, and the unequivocal condemnation of terrorist attacks and hostage-taking. However, as Council President, Brazil remains convinced that only a text capable of building genuine consensus can overcome the Council's paralysis and effectively address the catastrophic humanitarian emergency on the ground. As this draft does not bridge the profound divisions within the Council, Brazil cannot support it and will abstain.
messages.China: China fully supports this draft resolution. It reflects the overwhelming call of the international community, particularly the Arab world, for an immediate cessation of hostilities, the protection of civilians, and the urgent alleviation of the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. We commend the penholder's efforts to craft a balanced, responsible text and urge the Council to act decisively without delay.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador welcomes the incorporation of our proposals into revision 1, notably the unequivocal condemnation of the terrorist attacks committed by Hamas, the explicit affirmation of the right of self-defence under Article 51 of the Charter, and the call for urgent humanitarian pauses. The text now presents a balanced approach that addresses both the immediate humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza and the legitimate security and legal concerns of all parties. In the spirit of multilateral compromise and the urgent need for Council action to protect civilian lives, Ecuador supports the adoption of this draft resolution.
messages.France: France welcomes the penholder's constructive incorporation of key elements, notably the recognition of the right to self-defence in line with the UN Charter and the explicit condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks. However, calling for an immediate ceasefire remains unacceptable as it would restrict Israel's ability to protect its population against ongoing terror threats. The Council must remain focused on urgent, strictly observed humanitarian pauses to ensure civilian protection, rapid aid delivery, and the unconditional release of all hostages.
messages.Gabon: Gabon fully supports the draft resolution as revised. The text strikes an essential balance by firmly condemning the heinous terrorist attacks of 7 October, demanding the unconditional release of all hostages, and prioritizing the protection of civilians and unhindered humanitarian assistance in Gaza. Given the catastrophic humanitarian situation on the ground, the Security Council cannot remain paralyzed and must act decisively to alleviate human suffering.
messages.Ghana: Ghana appreciates the penholder's constructive engagement and the incorporation of our suggestions regarding humanitarian pauses and adherence to international humanitarian law. However, as Ghana has consistently maintained, it is vital that the Security Council speaks with one unified voice rather than advancing competing, divisive texts that fail to bridge differences among members. In the absence of broad consensus across the Council, Ghana cannot support the adoption of this draft resolution and will abstain.
messages.Japan: Japan appreciates the penholder's efforts to accommodate our concerns, including the reference to Article 51 and the explicit condemnation of Hamas's heinous terrorist attacks. To ensure the Council speaks with one voice and produces a workable outcome on the ground, OP1 should focus squarely on humanitarian pauses rather than a premature ceasefire that overlooks the security realities and ongoing hostage crisis. Furthermore, the text should acknowledge and reinforce the intensive diplomatic efforts currently underway to secure hostage releases and expand humanitarian access.
messages.Malta: Malta appreciates the penholder's efforts to incorporate explicit condemnation of Hamas' terrorist attacks and a reference to self-defence under Article 51. However, the text as currently drafted still lacks the necessary balance to unite the Council, notably the explicit reaffirmation of Israel's right to defend itself in strict compliance with international humanitarian law and stronger language on the protection of children. Without genuine Council unity and a balanced framework, Malta cannot support the resolution and will abstain.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the draft resolution as presented. The text strikes an appropriate balance by demanding the protection of civilians, the unhindered delivery of life-saving humanitarian assistance, and the release of hostages, while reaffirming the two-State solution. Given the catastrophic and rapidly deteriorating situation on the ground in Gaza, it is imperative that the Security Council act decisively and speak with one voice.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland thanks the penholder for accommodating our proposals in this revised draft, notably the unequivocal condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks, the inclusion of fundamental international humanitarian law principles, and the call for urgent humanitarian pauses. This text now strikes the necessary balance between addressing the catastrophic humanitarian emergency in Gaza, demanding the immediate release of hostages, and upholding compliance with international law and the protection of civilians. Switzerland is ready to vote in favour and urges all Council members to support this text so the Security Council can finally speak with one voice.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates supports the draft resolution as presented. The text strikes a necessary balance by demanding urgent humanitarian pauses leading to a durable ceasefire, calling for the rescission of the evacuation order, securing the delivery of vital aid—including fuel—and ensuring the protection of all civilians and the unconditional release of hostages. In light of the unfolding catastrophe in Gaza, the Security Council cannot afford further inaction, and we urge all members to support this text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support this draft in its current form. A call for a ceasefire at this stage would simply allow Hamas to entrench its positions, regroup, and continue its campaign of terror against Israeli civilians. We also cannot support calls in paragraph 6 to rescind evacuation advisories aimed at moving civilians out of harm's way, nor the persistent failure to explicitly hold Hamas accountable for its widespread use of human shields.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support a resolution that calls for or leads to a ceasefire, which at this stage would only serve to leave Hamas in place, capable of regrouping and perpetrating the atrocities of October 7 all over again. Furthermore, the Council must not attempt to micromanage Israel's military response by demanding the rescission of evacuation warnings intended to move civilians out of harm's way. Unless these critical issues are resolved, the United States will oppose this draft.

steps.summary: Revision 2 eliminates the red-line triggers of the United States and the United Kingdom by removing the ceasefire language from OP1 and deleting the call to rescind evacuation warnings in OP6, while integrating Japan's paragraph on diplomatic initiatives and the UK's language on human shields. These pragmatic adjustments preserve essential civilian protection provisions and unhindered humanitarian aid delivery while pre-empting any permanent member veto. As a result, the resolution achieves the broad cross-regional support required for adoption by the Security Council.

reasons.Albania: Despite the inclusion of essential language condemning Hamas and recognizing Israel's right to self-defence, Albania aligns with its key transatlantic allies and abstains on the Russian-led draft due to broader concerns over the penholder's balance and approach, reserving our substantive remarks for after the vote.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil previously sought a balanced compromise through its own presidential initiative and maintains an abstention on competing text proposals that fail to reflect a genuine Council consensus. In line with its position during consultations, Brazil abstains on this draft.
reasons.China: China consistently supports efforts to achieve an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, protect civilians, and alleviate the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, in line with our support for previous Russian-led initiatives.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the draft resolution as it explicitly condemns the Hamas terrorist attacks, recognizes Israel's right to self-defence under Article 51, upholds international humanitarian law, and calls for urgent humanitarian pauses and the release of hostages, addressing the core requirements previously articulated by our delegation.
reasons.France: The draft resolution incorporates France's essential requirements: unequivocal condemnation of the terrorist attacks by Hamas, recognition of Israel's right to defend itself in accordance with international humanitarian law, a demand for the immediate release of hostages, and urgent humanitarian pauses rather than an unfeasible immediate ceasefire. Having seen our proposed amendments accepted to produce a balanced humanitarian text, France votes in favour.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon has consistently voted in favour of all draft resolutions aimed at alleviating the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, establishing humanitarian pauses, condemning terrorism, and securing the release of hostages, and will maintain its practice of explaining its vote after the ballot.
reasons.Ghana: Consistent with Ghana's established position on competing draft resolutions that lack consensus among Council members, and in line with our position in the negotiation round, Ghana abstains on this text.
reasons.Japan: Our key proposals—replacing the call for a ceasefire with humanitarian pauses and explicitly endorsing ongoing diplomatic efforts led by the United States, Egypt, and Qatar—were fully accepted by the penholder. As the text also reaffirms Israel's right to defend its territory and people under international law and unequivocally condemns Hamas's terrorist attacks and hostage-taking, Japan votes in favour.
reasons.Malta: While Malta appreciates the incorporation of our language regarding self-defence and the protection of children and women, the draft resolution lacks the necessary broad Council consensus and balance, leading Malta to maintain its abstention.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique consistently supports Council action to protect civilians, secure unhindered humanitarian access, and de-escalate the conflict, aligning with its affirmative stance during negotiations.
reasons.Russian Federation: As the primary author and sponsor of the draft resolution, the Russian Federation naturally votes in favour and takes the floor before the vote to introduce the text and urge Council members to support it.
reasons.Switzerland: The draft resolution incorporates Switzerland's core priorities—including the unequivocal condemnation of Hamas' terrorist acts, full respect for international humanitarian law, the release of hostages, and urgent humanitarian pauses—warranting a vote in favour. In line with Council practice, Switzerland reserves its explanation of vote for after the voting procedure.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates votes in favour of the draft resolution in line with its consistent position supporting urgent humanitarian pauses, unhindered aid delivery to civilians in Gaza, and the immediate release of hostages, reserving its remarks for after the vote.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom opposes this Russian-drafted resolution as it falls short of properly reflecting Israel's inherent right to defend itself and fails to provide a credible, balanced basis for Council action, aligning with our coordination with the United States.
reasons.United States of America: The United States opposes Russian-led initiatives on this file, viewing them as cynical and uncoordinated with on-the-ground diplomacy, and objects to language condemning Israeli military actions without giving full, uncompromised backing to Israel's right to self-defence.

before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President, 

The Security Council cannot remain paralyzed while a catastrophe of unprecedented proportions unfolds in the Gaza Strip. Every minute of delay costs human lives. Thousands of civilians, predominantly women and children, have already been killed, civilian infrastructure is being systematically reduced to rubble, and the humanitarian system is on the brink of total collapse due to the acute lack of fuel, water, food, and medical supplies.

The draft resolution before us today is aimed squarely at stopping this humanitarian disaster, ensuring the urgent delivery of relief to those in desperate need, and securing the unconditional release of hostages. It is a balanced, action-oriented text that reflects the urgent imperatives of international humanitarian law. We urge all members of the Security Council to act responsibly, abandon narrow geopolitical calculations, and vote in favour of this draft resolution.
before.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. While Russia has attempted to make cosmetic adjustments to its text, this draft remains fundamentally flawed and insincere. Russia did not engage in good faith consultations, nor does this resolution reflect the reality on the ground or support the sensitive, direct diplomacy currently being conducted by the United States and regional partners to secure the release of hostages and open sustainable humanitarian corridors. Moreover, this draft continues to contain unacceptable language that undermines Israel’s inherent right to defend itself against Hamas terrorism while drawing false equivalences. We urge Council members to vote against this draft and instead support the text put forward by the United States, which offers a practical, balanced path forward.

after.Albania:
Mr. President,

Albania abstained in the vote on the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. 

Our position on this crisis has been consistent, clear, and principled from day one. We have repeatedly stated that this Council must act with moral clarity and responsibility. 

First, we cannot lose sight of how this latest cycle of violence started. On 7 October, Hamas unleashed monstrous, barbaric terrorist attacks against innocent Israeli civilians. No cause, no grievance can ever justify such atrocities. Hamas is a terrorist organization, and its actions must be unequivocally condemned as terrorism, without hesitation, caveats, or false equivalences. 

Second, every sovereign State has the inherent right to defend itself and protect its people against terror, in full conformity with international law, including international humanitarian law. 

Third, the protection of civilians must be paramount at all times. The suffering of innocent Palestinian civilians in Gaza is heartbreaking and unbearable. International humanitarian law must be respected by all parties, humanitarian aid—food, water, medicine, and fuel—must flow rapidly and unhindered to those in desperate need, and humanitarian pauses must be enabled. Furthermore, all hostages held by Hamas must be released immediately and unconditionally.

Albania abstained today because we believe that any text adopted by this Council must reflect these essential principles in a balanced and genuine manner. A draft resolution should not be brought forward merely as a political exercise or to score points, but rather to foster genuine Council unity and to tangibly support the critical and delicate diplomatic efforts being carried out on the ground by key international and regional partners, notably the United States, Egypt, and Qatar, to secure the release of hostages and alleviate humanitarian suffering.

Only by standing firm against terrorism, upholding international humanitarian law, and remaining committed to a negotiated two-State solution can we hope to bring an end to this tragic conflict and ensure a future of peace, security, and dignity for both Israelis and Palestinians.

Thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution just put to the vote. We express our deep regret and disappointment that, despite receiving the support of the majority of Council members, including Arab and developing countries, the draft resolution was once again not adopted due to the use of the veto.

The current situation in Gaza is deteriorating at an alarming speed and has already evolved into an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe. Over the past two weeks, intense bombardments have caused massive civilian casualties, a vast number of whom are women and children. Essential supplies of water, electricity, fuel, and food have been cut off, hospitals and medical infrastructure are on the brink of total collapse, and millions of innocent civilians are trapped in extreme despair and peril. 

China condemns all violence and attacks against civilians and opposes all violations of international law. We reiterate that international humanitarian law must be scrupulously observed by all parties under all circumstances. Civilians, hospitals, schools, and humanitarian facilities must never become military targets. The collective punishment of the people of Gaza cannot be justified on any grounds and must be stopped immediately. 

The draft resolution put to the vote today reflected the urgent and widespread call of the international community, particularly the Arab world, for an immediate humanitarian pause, the unhindered delivery of emergency humanitarian assistance, the lifting of the siege on Gaza, and the unconditional release of all civilian hostages. It represented an important effort by the Council to fulfill its responsibility under the Charter of the United Nations to maintain international peace and security and protect human lives. At this critical juncture, every hour of inaction costs innocent lives. Allowing the conflict to expand and escalate will only lead to greater disaster and drag the entire region into an abyss.

Mr. President,

The root cause of the prolonged and recurring conflict between Palestine and Israel lies in the fact that the legitimate national rights of the Palestinian people have not been realized and that the two-State solution has not been implemented. To end this vicious cycle of violence, the international community must uphold an objective and just stance, act with moral conscience, and take concrete steps to de-escalate the conflict and revive the two-State solution on the basis of relevant United Nations resolutions.

China will continue to firmly stand on the side of peace, justice, and international law, and work tirelessly with regional countries and the international community to bring an immediate end to the hostilities, protect civilians, alleviate the humanitarian crisis, and realize a comprehensive, just, and lasting settlement of the question of Palestine.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Ecuador:
Mr. President,

Ecuador voted in favour of the draft resolution that was just put to the vote because it addressed the fundamental concerns that my delegation had previously expressed in this Council, reflecting the urgent priorities required by the catastrophic situation on the ground.

My delegation has maintained a principled and consistent position throughout our deliberations. As we stated previously, the Council could not remain indifferent nor adopt texts that failed to condemn the heinous terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas on 7 October, which triggered this grave escalation, or that ignored the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. 

At the same time, this draft resolution placed the protection of civilians and scrupulous compliance with international law, in particular international humanitarian law, at the center of our collective response. The catastrophic humanitarian crisis in the Gaza Strip—where civilians, especially women and children, are suffering unimaginable deprivation of water, food, fuel, electricity, and medical supplies—demands urgent and extended humanitarian pauses to enable safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access.

We deeply regret that, once again, the Security Council has been unable to shoulder its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security due to the use of the veto. The continuing paralysis of this Council does not diminish the suffering of civilians in Israel or in the occupied Palestinian territory; rather, it undermines the credibility of this body at a moment when leadership and collective action are most urgently required.

Ecuador will continue to work constructively with all members of the Council and regional partners to achieve an immediate de-escalation of violence, secure the unconditional release of all hostages, ensure vital humanitarian relief reaches those in desperate need, and revive the political path towards a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution, where Israel and Palestine can live side by side within secure and recognized borders.

Thank you.
after.France:
France voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted today. 

Faced with the dramatic escalation of violence and the humanitarian catastrophe unfolding before our eyes, it was imperative for the Security Council to finally overcome its divisions and speak with one voice. 

France has maintained a consistent and principled position since the beginning of this crisis. First, we have unequivocally condemned the heinous terrorist attacks perpetrated by Hamas against Israel and its people on 7 October. Nothing can ever justify such atrocities. Israel has an inherent right to defend itself and its citizens against terror, but it must do so in strict compliance with international law, in particular international humanitarian law and the principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution. The protection of all civilians, whether Israeli or Palestinian, is a legal and moral obligation.

Second, France continues to demand the immediate, safe, and unconditional release of all hostages held by Hamas in Gaza. We think of them and their families, and we commend the mediation efforts underway to secure their freedom.

Third, the humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip is catastrophic and demands urgent, decisive action. The civilian population of Gaza cannot be held collectively responsible for the crimes committed by Hamas. Rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access is urgently required, along with humanitarian pauses, to allow the delivery of essential supplies—water, food, medicine, and fuel—to civilians in dire need, as well as the protection of humanitarian workers and medical infrastructure.

Finally, we must prevent any regional conflagration and urgently work toward a political horizon. Only the two-State solution, with two democratic States living side by side in peace and security along the 1967 lines, can bring a just and lasting peace to Israelis and Palestinians.

France deeply regrets that the Council was once again unable to adopt a resolution today. We will continue our efforts, together with all our partners, to ensure that this Council fully assumes its responsibilities to protect civilians and promote peace and security.
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan voted in favour of the draft resolution just put to the vote. 

Our vote reflects our grave and growing concern over the catastrophic humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip. Innocent civilians, including a vast number of children, women, and the elderly, are suffering immensely from acute shortages of water, food, electricity, fuel, and essential medical supplies. The humanitarian system is on the verge of collapse. Japan has consistently stated that we are second to none in caring about the humanitarian situation on the ground and the human dignity of all civilians, both Palestinians and Israelis. Safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access, including through humanitarian pauses, is urgently needed to deliver life-saving aid to those in desperate need.

At the same time, Japan has unequivocally and repeatedly condemned the heinous terror attacks committed by Hamas and other militants against Israel. Nothing can justify such acts of terror. We demand the immediate, safe, and unconditional release of all hostages who are still being held captive. 

Japan recognizes that Israel has the right to defend itself and its people in accordance with international law. In doing so, all parties must scrupulously comply with their obligations under international law, including international humanitarian law, and uphold the principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution. The protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure must be paramount under all circumstances.

We also stress the vital importance of preventing any regional spillover of this conflict. Japan continues to strongly support and appreciate the tireless, on-the-ground diplomatic efforts being conducted by the United States, Egypt, Qatar, and other regional and international partners to secure the release of hostages, facilitate humanitarian corridors, and de-escalate tensions.

Finally, we must not lose sight of the horizon for peace. Japan remains steadfast in its commitment to a two-State solution, where Israel and an independent Palestinian State live side by side in peace and security. Japan will continue to actively engage in diplomatic efforts to improve the humanitarian situation, protect innocent lives, and help bring stability to the region as quickly as possible.

Thank you, Mr. President.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

We deeply regret that the Security Council has once again fallen hostage to the narrow, selfish geopolitical interests of the United States and the United Kingdom. 

Today, nine members of the Security Council—representing different regions of the world—voted in favour of our draft resolution, which was aimed solely at stopping the bloodshed, establishing humanitarian pauses, protecting civilians, and securing the unconditional release of hostages. The text met the threshold required for adoption. However, it was cynically torpedoed by the vetoes of Washington and London.

By casting their negative votes, the United States and the United Kingdom have sent an unmistakable signal: they do not want the violence to stop. They bear direct responsibility for preventing the Security Council from fulfilling its primary mandate under the United Nations Charter to maintain international peace and security. Under the guise of spurious procedural arguments and false claims, they have once again provided a political cover to continue the collective punishment and destruction of the civilian population of the Gaza Strip.

The hypocrisy of our Western colleagues has been laid bare for the entire world to see. While preaching the protection of human rights and international humanitarian law elsewhere, they blatantly disregard the catastrophic suffering and loss of life of thousands of Palestinian civilians, including children and women, deprived of the most basic necessities of life.

Russia will continue its active and principled efforts, together with regional and international partners, to put an end to this violence, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, and revive a genuine political process leading to a viable two-State solution on the universally recognized international legal basis.

Thank you.
after.Switzerland:
Mr. President,

Switzerland voted in favour of the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. We deeply regret that, once again, the Security Council has been unable to overcome its divisions and adopt a resolution in response to the dramatic crisis unfolding in the Middle East.

Since 7 October, Switzerland has unequivocally condemned the heinous acts of terror, indiscriminate rocket attacks and the taking of hostages perpetrated by Hamas against the Israeli population. We demand the immediate and unconditional release of all civilian hostages and insist that their humane treatment be ensured in accordance with international law. We recognize Israel’s right to ensure its defence and security, underscoring that this right must be exercised in strict compliance with international law, in particular international humanitarian law.

At the same time, Switzerland is profoundly alarmed by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in the Gaza Strip. Thousands of civilians, the vast majority of them women and children, have lost their lives, and the civilian population is deprived of the most essential supplies—water, electricity, food, medical supplies, and fuel. 

International humanitarian law must be respected by all parties, at all times, without exception. The principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution in the conduct of hostilities are paramount. Civilians, medical personnel, and humanitarian workers—including United Nations staff who are carrying out life-saving work at tremendous personal risk—must be protected, along with hospitals and civilian infrastructure.

Switzerland supported this draft resolution because it reflected these urgent imperatives: it condemned terrorism and the attacks by Hamas, demanded the release of all hostages, and called for urgent and extended humanitarian pauses to allow rapid, safe, and unhindered humanitarian access throughout the Gaza Strip.

Faced with this immense human suffering, the Council cannot remain paralyzed. Switzerland will continue to support all efforts aimed at rapid de-escalation, ensuring respect for international humanitarian law, securing the release of hostages, and establishing safe humanitarian corridors. Finally, we reiterate that only a negotiated two-State solution, where Israel and Palestine live side by side in peace and security within recognized borders, will provide a just and lasting foundation for peace in the region.

Thank you.
after.United Arab Emirates:
Thank you, Mr. President.

The United Arab Emirates voted in favour of the draft resolution put forward today because it responded to the most urgent, basic, and non-negotiable imperative facing this Council: addressing the catastrophic and rapidly deteriorating humanitarian disaster in the Gaza Strip.

Every passing hour of inaction by this Council carries a terrible human cost. In Gaza today, water, fuel, food, and essential medical supplies are running out. Hospitals are on the verge of total collapse, doctors are being forced to operate without anesthesia, and over two million civilians are trapped in a living nightmare with nowhere safe to turn. The United Nations and humanitarian agencies have warned us repeatedly and unequivocally that Gaza is running out of life. 

We have been clear and consistent from the outset: we unequivocally condemn the heinous attacks committed by Hamas on 7 October and the taking of hostages, and we demand their immediate and unconditional release. But international humanitarian law is absolute. It does not permit collective punishment, and it does not allow the starvation, siege, or indiscriminate bombardment of an entire civilian population. 

This Council cannot afford to be paralyzed by geopolitical division while thousands of innocent lives, the vast majority of them women and children, are being extinguished. Our vote in favour reflects our steadfast belief that the Security Council must fulfill its mandate under the Charter of the United Nations. We must demand humanitarian pauses that allow life-saving aid to flow at scale, ensure the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, and prevent this conflict from engulfing the wider region.

We deeply regret that the Council has once again failed to act unitedly today. The United Arab Emirates will continue to work tirelessly with all Council members and regional partners to alleviate the immense suffering of civilians in Gaza and to preserve the viability of a two-State solution where Palestinians and Israelis can finally live side by side in peace and security.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom voted against this draft resolution. Once again, Russia has failed to consult in good faith and has shown no serious interest in building consensus within this Council. 

This Council must approach the crisis with seriousness and unity of purpose. We must be unequivocal in condemning the barbaric terrorist attacks committed by Hamas on 7 October, which resulted in the murder of more than 1,400 people and the taking of over 200 hostages. We must also reaffirm Israel’s inherent right to defend itself against terrorism, in line with international humanitarian law.

At the same time, the humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic and deteriorating rapidly. Innocent Palestinian civilians are suffering terribly. We urgently need to see life-saving humanitarian aid—food, water, medicine, and fuel—delivered at scale to those in desperate need. We support specific humanitarian pauses to allow aid to enter and to facilitate the safe and unconditional release of all hostages held by Hamas. 

Instead of cynical political posturing, this Council needs genuine diplomatic engagement. The United Kingdom will continue to work closely with international and regional partners to alleviate the humanitarian suffering in Gaza, secure the release of all hostages, and prevent any wider regional escalation.
